title: Session-centric billing sandbox
content:
Quick personal scratchpad — exploring session-centric billing as an alternative to pure per-token or per-request pricing. Keep this messy; want to capture instincts and rough math for next sync with Samir/Lina.

Goal / motivation:
- Simpler UX for developers building chat/session experiences: price per active session minute or per session handle rather than raw tokens.
- Smooths revenue predictability and helps align cost model with concurrency/bandwidth characteristics (latency-sensitive apps).
- Potential to encourage longer-lived sessions (stickiness) while still preserving incentive to batch/compact prompts.

High-level idea:
- Charge a small base per session-open (cover routing/metadata overhead) + a per-minute or per-1,000-token equivalent rate while session is active. Include a burst credit for initial messages to account for long system prompts.
- Cap session charges or switch to per-token pricing after X tokens to avoid punishment for heavy single sessions.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Model cost (RWD XL-ish) delivered: $0.30 per 1M output tokens equivalent (hosted marginal cost, incl infra amortized).
- Average prompt+completion ratio: 1.3 tokens in prompt per 1 token out (so total tokens = 2.3x output tokens roughly). Use 2.0x to be conservative.
- Avg tokens per message (user+model): 250 tokens roundtrip (short chat).
- Average session length: 12 minutes active (multiple messages).
- Active messages per minute: ~1.5 (frequent back-and-forth).

Derive per-minute token equivalent:
- messages/minute * tokens/message = 1.5 * 250 = 375 tokens/minute
- cost per token = $0.30 / 1,000,000 = $3e-7 per token
- cost per minute = 375 * 3e-7 = $0.0001125 (~$0.00011)
- per hour = *60 = $0.00675 (~$0.0068/hr)

UX price anchors we can test (gross margins aim 60-75%):
- If cost/hr = $0.0068, to achieve 70% gross margin, price/hr = cost / 0.3 = $0.0227 ≈ $0.023/hr (~$0.000383/min)
- Translate to per-session: for 12 min average, price/session ≈ $0.276. That feels high vs expectations for small consumer apps, but acceptable for enterprise/scale apps.

Alternate simpler slab: per-session buckets (good for PLG):
- Tiny session: up to 50 tokens => free (or included in free tier)
- Short session: up to 1k tokens => $0.05 per session
- Medium session: up to 5k tokens => $0.18 per session
- Long session: up to 20k tokens => $0.60 per session
- Overage: per-token charge of $0.00000035 (slightly higher than infra)

Rationale: slabs provide predictability and easy billing UI; overage prevents abuse. Need to simulate revenue against real distribution.

Session vs per-token tradeoffs:
- Pros of session model:
  - Easier mental model for product teams building chat (price = sessions * multiplier).
  - Aligns with concurrency and routing costs (many small messages cause routing overhead).
  - Can include smart caps & free bursts to avoid punishing short tests.
- Cons:
  - Harder to price for massively long LLM usage (coding assistants, editors).
  - Risk of users gaming session boundaries (open multiple sessions).
  - Adds state tracking overhead (session lifecycle, heartbeats).

Edge cases and mitigations:
- Idle sessions with periodic heartbeats: define 'active' = last user msg within N minutes (e.g., 2m), charge only when active.
- Bots that poll every second: debounce by counting messages per minute with an upper bound for billing calculations.
- Shared sessions across users (collaborative docs): prorate per seat or use seat+session hybrid.

Hybrid proposal (simple):
- Free tier: 50 free session-minutes per month (or 10 free short sessions).
- Pay-as-you-go sessions: $0.02 per session-minute (intro anchor) with monthly volume discounts.
- For heavy usage (>100k tokens/session or >1k min/month) auto-convert to per-token billing at a negotiated rate.
- Dedicated customers: ability to pin per-session price + capacity commit (similar to Dedicated reserved capacity).

Quick examples (concrete):
- Consumer chat app, 10k MAU, avg 2 sessions/month, avg 12 min/session => monthly minutes = 240k. Price @ $0.02/min => revenue = $4,800/month. Cost to us = 240k * $0.0001125 = $27 => huge gross margin. Means we can price cheaper and still profitable.
- Enterprise support product, 2.5k agents, high activity (avg 60 min/day agent) => 2.5k * 60 * 30 = 4.5M minutes/month. Cost = 4.5M * 0.0001125 = $506.25/month. Wait math seems off; check steps: 4.5M * 0.0001125 = $506.25 — yes low, suspiciously low relative to expected cloud costs. Need to validate model cost assumption (likely undercounting GPU/time amortization + other infra).

Important sanity check: our base assumption ($0.30 per 1M tokens) probably reflects highly optimized inference. For hosted public model with egress, overheads, SRE, support, we should multiply by 4–7x for True COGS. Use $1.2 per 1M tokens as conservative. Recalc quickly:
- cost/token = $1.2 / 1e6 = 1.2e-6
- cost/min = 375 * 1.2e-6 = $0.00045/min
- cost/hr = $0.027/hr
- For 240k minutes => cost = 240k * 0.00045 = $108/month (still low)
- For 4.5M min => cost = 4.5M * 0.00045 = $2,025/month (again seems low).

Conclusion: token-only COGS seems lower than expected because tokens are cheap at scale; main fixed costs (instances, GPUs idling, routing infra, storage, licensing) dominate for some customers. So session pricing can capture fixed costs via base session fee.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need to run simulation on real usage histogram (per-customer session length distribution). Request dataset from analytics: per-session tokens, messages/min, active-minutes distribution. -> JIRA ENG-3421 is the request.
- Design UI/SDK: how do we instrument "session open/close"? Suggested SDK calls: startSession(metadata), heartbeat(), endSession(). Also server-side heuristics for orphaned sessions.
- Anti-abuse: rate limits on session opens, min billable granularity (e.g., 30s).
- Billing pipeline changes: add session-minute metric to usage export (BigQuery schema change). Need to coordinate with finance.

Potential experiments (A/B):
A) Offer session pricing to a cohort of chat apps (self-serve) and measure ARPU, conversion from free tier.
B) Offer per-token vs session for same traffic and compare stickiness and cost per session for customers.

Notes to self before sending to Samir/Lina:
- Pull 90-day sample of sessions from analytics; compute median/90p tokens per session.
- Validate infra COGS per token using infra-cost model (ask Infra for up-to-date $/token calc).
- Draft UX copy for console: "Sessions: billed per active minute. Free 50 trial minutes/month."

Random ideas worth saving:
- Offer "session bundles" prepaid: e.g., 1k session-minutes = $X with rollover. Useful for SMBs.
- Seat + session hybrid for collaboration tools: seats pay monthly, sessions pay variable.
- Use session pricing to nudge customers toward longer-lived websocket connections and fewer re-open overheads (win for infra).

Last line: keep this as sandbox, run numbers with real analytics before writing into pricing book.

End of scratchpad.
